The fair comparison is the rule with the same 15 drinks and Wednesday runs: $837.99. With only the first five drinks, the rule made $443.09.

What we learned, and what we changed

Lessons for the prompt, rules and tools.

Fixed · round 2It skipped the day-one fill

No receipts looked like "contents unknown", so week 1 sold nothing. The rules card now says the machine starts empty, and the season ends Wed 3 Feb.

Fixed · round 2Thursday missed Amazon's cutoff

Restocks landed Monday. The prompt now gives each store's cutoff, and the runs moved to Wednesday.

Fixed · round 3It refilled only once slots were empty

The new top-up rule refills a slot before it would run out by the visit after next. Every slot sold.

Fixed · round 3 (#137)Only five drinks could be bought

With the team's 15 Nov sourcing it stocked 13 drinks in 20 slots, at most 2 slots of any one.

Open · budgetRuns cost more with more drinks

$0.31 to $0.77 a run. A $4.50 season cap ran out on 20 Jan and lost 121 units; a season needs about $5.

Open · team decisionThe wildcard slot

One slot up to $8.00 for a riskier bet. Built and reviewed on add_wildcard_slot; #110 item 1.

Why the agent won

Same drinks as the rule, but it topped up before slots ran out, tested two $0.25 rises, and skipped buying on the last day.

The caveat

Each new drink's demand is borrowed from the fall. More drinks may help less than the simulator says, so read the gap over the rule, not the total.

For the team to decide

The wildcard slot (#110 item 1), and the run day: Wednesday meets Amazon's cutoff; keep a run on go-live day, Thu 3 Dec.
